doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Writing 'A Dog' for her Yorkie FiFi
summary: She wrote the tune after the dog died, and bandmates at a Town Hall concert struggled with its odd four-four.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No kidding. That’s funny. When you write a tune like that, earlier on we had kind of talked about this, is it a result of sitting --
The dog died. So in the evening I’d begin to feel bad and I thought okay I’m going to write a tune for him. And the tune came right out.

Very, very simple, but it sounds just exactly like the dog. And it’s in four four, which I think is not a problem, but there was a Town Hall concert we played that Randy Brecker and Dave Liebman were the horn players and Pat Martino was on guitar. And they were trying to get this tune. And it was like, no, no, you wrote it wrong, no that’s not four four.
And finally they said yeah it is, but what is this? I never thought of it that way but that’s how the dog was, so you know you would never know what he was going to do next.
Wow. You really captured it, huh?
He was just off the wall. Yeah.
